what.a: SofraPiwas is a restaurant platform for QR menus, online ordering, reservations, loyalty and staff order workflows. A companion app can connect compatible network ESC/POS printers. Modules and hardware depend on each restaurant's setup. RUMI in Geneva is our reference restaurant.

pricing.a: Choose your modules, guest languages, look and currency in the plan builder to see your monthly EUR price before applicable VAT. No card is needed to request an account. Your subscription starts only when you start it from your dashboard.

payments.q: Can my guests pay online — including TWINT?
payments.a: Online payments is an optional module. The plan builder offers €19/month flat, or €9/month plus 1.5% of each online order. VAT may apply. Supported payment methods and activation depend on your market and Stripe setup; ask us to confirm availability before you rely on a specific method. TWINT is not currently confirmed as available, so ask us before relying on it.

languages.q: Which languages does the SofraPiwas guest interface support?
languages.a: The guest interface offers ten language options: English, French, German, Dutch, Italian, Spanish, Turkish, Arabic, Russian and Chinese. Menu content is translated only where a restaurant has published that language version, so check catalogue coverage before enabling a language.

printing.q: Can SofraPiwas connect to my kitchen printer?
printing.a: The companion app supports network ESC/POS printers on Windows and Android. Confirm your printer model, network and physical setup during onboarding before relying on printed kitchen tickets.

who.q: Who is behind SofraPiwas, and is it actually used anywhere?
who.a: SofraPiwas is built by a small team based in the Netherlands. RUMI is our Geneva reference restaurant; its public menu and table-reservation pages run on SofraPiwas. Staff workflows, printer hardware and menu translation coverage should be checked for each restaurant setup. We onboard new restaurants personally.

domain.q: Can I use my own domain name?
domain.a: Yes. Every restaurant gets a free sofra subdomain, and you can connect a domain you already own — or we register a brand-new one for you during setup.

meta.title: SofraPiwas vs GloriaFood (2026): pricing, features & transition
meta.description: Compare current features, prices and support dates for SofraPiwas and GloriaFood. GloriaFood has announced service end on 30 April 2027; sources checked 30 September 2026.

compare.label: Side by side
compare.title: SofraPiwas vs GloriaFood
compare.subtitle: Two honest ways to put a restaurant online — compared fairly, with sources and a date.
compare.intro1: GloriaFood — part of Oracle — lists a free core product with optional paid modules. SofraPiwas is a Netherlands-built restaurant platform. In Geneva, RUMI's public menu, online ordering and table-reservation pages run on SofraPiwas; other staff workflows and hardware are configured for each restaurant.
compare.intro2: The right fit depends on your setup and how long you need the service. GloriaFood has announced an end-of-life date; if you use it, include a transition plan in your comparison.

table.caption: SofraPiwas and GloriaFood, feature by feature

pricing.label: Pricing model
pricing.sofra: Core starts at €19/month. Choose modules, guest languages, look and currency to see your monthly EUR price in the plan builder, before applicable VAT. No card is needed to request an account; billing starts only when you start a subscription from your dashboard.
pricing.gf: Current listing: free core with no monthly fee or commission per order; paid modules include online payments (US$29/month), advanced promotions (US$19/month), and POS (US$49/month per location, two-year commitment). GloriaFood has announced service end on 30 April 2027.

ordering.label: QR & online ordering
ordering.sofra: Included — QR menus at the table and online ordering, with photos, allergens and customizations. No app to install.
ordering.gf: Included free — ordering widget for your website and Facebook page, plus QR dine-in ordering.

reservations.label: Table reservations
reservations.sofra: Included — online booking, table planning, working hours, one-tap approval.
reservations.gf: Reservation widget included; taking booking deposits costs US$0.50 per guest on accepted bookings.

loyalty.label: Loyalty & promotions
loyalty.sofra: Included — fidelity points plus discount rules per customer group.
loyalty.gf: Promotions and coupons in the free plan; the advanced promo-marketing module costs US$19/month.

printing.label: Kitchen printing
printing.sofra: A Windows and Android companion app supports network ESC/POS printers. Confirm printer compatibility and installation for your restaurant before relying on printed tickets.
printing.gf: Their free order-taking app (Android and iOS) connects to a thermal printer and prints accepted orders automatically.

languages.label: Languages
languages.sofra: The guest interface offers ten language options. Menu-item text appears in the translations available for that menu; check your catalogue coverage before publishing each language.
languages.gf: GloriaFood says its system is available in widely used languages, with more added by community contributors. Its cited page does not give a fixed language count.

hosting.label: Hosting & domains
hosting.sofra: Runs on SofraPiwas-managed infrastructure in the EU; every restaurant gets its own domain — yours, or one we register for you.
hosting.gf: Cloud service operated by Oracle (GloriaFood is an Oracle product).

setup.label: Setup & support
setup.sofra: Personal onboarding: we configure your menu, QR codes and agreed staff views with you. We confirm compatible printer hardware and setup before you rely on printed tickets.
setup.gf: Self-service — you set the system up yourself through their admin panel and documentation.

payments.label: Online payments
payments.sofra: Optional module: €19/month flat, or €9/month plus 1.5% of each online order. VAT may apply. Supported methods and activation depend on your market and Stripe setup; confirm availability during onboarding.
payments.gf: Available as a paid module — online / card payments at US$29/month.

compare.disclaimer: GloriaFood's features and prices were checked on 30 September 2026 against its public pages and may change. Its official notice says service ends on 30 April 2027 and support for existing customers continues through that date. Prices shown for GloriaFood are in US dollars, excluding taxes. GloriaFood is an Oracle product; names and trademarks belong to their owners.

free.a: GloriaFood's pricing page currently lists no monthly fee and no commission for its core ordering service. Paid options include online payments (US$29/month), advanced promotions (US$19/month), and POS (US$49/month per location, with a two-year commitment). GloriaFood has announced an end-of-life date of 30 April 2027, with support for existing customers through that date, so plan for a transition rather than treating the free tier as a long-term option.

cost.a: Core starts at €19/month. Select modules, guest languages, look and currency in the plan builder to see your monthly EUR price before applicable VAT. No card is needed to request an account; your subscription starts only when you start it from your dashboard.

pick.a: If you already use GloriaFood and its documented features meet your needs through the announced support period, you can keep using it while planning a move before 30 April 2027. If you want one system for ordering, reservations, loyalty and kitchen printing with personal setup, compare SofraPiwas' plan and onboarding against your requirements.

meta.title: Legal — imprint and privacy · SofraPiwas
meta.description: Who runs SofraPiwas, and how we handle your data.

imprint.title: Who we are
imprint.unset: Our registration details and contact address are not published here yet. They are on any invoice we have sent you.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.updated: This describes what the service actually does today, and is updated when that changes.

controller.title: Who is responsible
controller.body: The company named above is the controller for the data described here — the data of SofraPiwas's own customers and partners. This page does not cover a restaurant's own guests: their bookings and orders live in that restaurant's own installation, and that restaurant publishes its own privacy policy for them.

what.title: What we collect
what.body: For accounts: your name, email address and a password hash. For billing: your company's legal name, address, registration number, VAT number and billing email, together with payment records from our payment provider and what the VAT service returned when we checked your number. If you contact us or apply to the partner programme, whatever you write in the form, including a phone number and city if you give them. For a partner: the restaurants you introduce, their contact details and your notes on them. We keep security logs of sign-in attempts, which include the email address that was tried. We run no analytics and no advertising trackers.

why.title: Why
why.body: To give you an account, to bill you, and to issue the invoices the law requires us to issue. We check VAT numbers against the European Commission's VIES service so we can apply the right tax treatment, and we keep the reference of that check as evidence.

keep.title: How long we keep it
keep.body: Invoices, and the billing details printed on them, are kept for the period Dutch tax law requires. Sign-in and administrative logs are kept for 18 months. A partner application we turned down is kept for 12 months, then deleted. Sign-up invitation links expire and are deleted after 30 days. Accounts and CRM records are kept while the relationship lasts, and we remove them on request — there is no automatic clock on those. If your restaurant leaves us — including at the end of a free trial — we keep one encrypted backup of its data for 24 months, so you can pick up where you left off if you come back. You can ask us to delete it sooner and we will.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You can ask for a copy of your data, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it. Write to the address above and we will answer. Some things we cannot delete on request, and it is fairer to say so: an issued invoice and the legal details printed on it, because we are required to keep them; and security logs, until their 18 months are up.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: A session cookie when you are signed in, and a cookie remembering your language. Your light or dark preference is stored in your browser and never sent to us. No analytics or advertising cookies.

processors.title: Who else sees it
processors.body: We use a small number of suppliers, and each receives only what its job needs. We also check VAT numbers against the European Commission's VIES service, which means sending it the number you gave us.
processors.source: source code and builds — and, for each restaurant we set up, its name, city and administrator's email address, which are recorded in a private repository
processors.monitoring: error monitoring, so we find out when something breaks

terms.title: Terms
terms.body: We have no published terms of service yet. Until we do, what applies is what we agree with you in writing — ask us and we will confirm it.

meta.title: GloriaFood alternatives for Swiss restaurants (2026)
meta.description: A dated, source-linked comparison of SofraPiwas, FoodAmigos and Lightspeed for restaurants in Switzerland, including public pricing and checks before migrating from GloriaFood.

alternatives.label: Compare your options
alternatives.title: GloriaFood alternatives for Swiss restaurants
alternatives.subtitle: A dated comparison of three different routes: a Swiss-market POS, a migration option named by GloriaFood, and SofraPiwas for restaurants looking for setup help.
alternatives.intro: GloriaFood says its service ends on 30 April 2027 and that support for existing customers continues through that date. Oracle says it has no direct replacement and points customers to FoodAmigos. If you use GloriaFood, compare options against your own menu, service flow, payments, data and staff needs before changing live links.
alternatives.scopeNote: This is a source-led snapshot, not a ranking. Provider descriptions and migration promises are attributed to the provider that publishes them. Public pages reviewed did not confirm every vendor’s Switzerland availability, processing fees or contract terms; ask for a written, restaurant-specific offer.

table.title: Compare by operating fit
table.note: The claims below reflect vendor pages checked on {date}. Public list prices can change and may exclude add-ons or payment charges.
table.caption: A comparison of restaurant software options for Switzerland

sofra.name: SofraPiwas
sofra.fit: You want ordering, reservations and loyalty, with staff workflows configured for your restaurant and printer compatibility checked for your setup.
sofra.published: The public plan builder lists Core from €19/month and shows a monthly EUR total for the selected modules, guest languages, look and currency before applicable VAT. Requesting an account needs no card; billing starts only when you start a subscription in the dashboard.
sofra.verify: The published price is in EUR. Check the exact module mix, language setup, currency display and payment methods in your plan and onboarding.

foodAmigos.name: FoodAmigos — the GloriaFood-referred migration option
foodAmigos.fit: You already use GloriaFood and want to evaluate the migration provider Oracle currently names.
foodAmigos.published: FoodAmigos says its team can move a restaurant’s menu, website content, customer data and settings; it also advertises 0% commission. These are the provider’s own claims. The reviewed migration page does not publish a standard price.
foodAmigos.verify: The public pages reviewed did not establish availability in Switzerland, CHF pricing or local payment support. Get written confirmation of migration scope, export format, fees, payment methods, data handling and timing.

lightspeed.name: Lightspeed Restaurant
lightspeed.fit: You want to evaluate a restaurant POS with QR ordering in the Swiss market.
lightspeed.published: Its Swiss restaurant page advertises table and QR ordering with integrated payments including TWINT. The public price page lists Basic at CHF 89/month for one licence, with QR order/pay as an add-on, and Core at CHF 159/month for two licences, with QR order/pay included.
lightspeed.verify: Confirm the exact plan, hardware, QR add-ons, payment processor, transaction charges and contract terms in a current quote; the advertised monthly subscription is only one part of total cost.

transition.title: A low-risk GloriaFood transition checklist
transition.intro: Keep your current customer route available while you test its replacement. The announced end date is a planning boundary, not a reason to switch a working service without a rehearsal.

steps.inventory: List every live touchpoint and workflow: website buttons, QR codes by table, social and map links, reservations, delivery or pickup, payments, notifications, reports and kitchen printing.
steps.export: Ask GloriaFood what can be exported, in which format and until when. Request the menu, modifiers, photos, allergen notes, customer data and settings you need; verify the export before cancelling anything.
steps.pilot: Rebuild a representative menu and test it with staff on real phones. Check languages, prices, modifiers, order routing, receipts, payments and printer or kitchen display.
steps.cutover: Choose a quiet service window, update one customer link at a time, keep a staff fallback ready and monitor the first live orders before removing the old route.

endDate.a: GloriaFood’s current notice says the service reaches end of life on 30 April 2027 and that support for existing customers continues through that date. Recheck its official notice before making a migration schedule.

foodAmigos.q: Is FoodAmigos a direct Oracle replacement for GloriaFood?
foodAmigos.a: No direct replacement is offered, according to Oracle’s notice. It names FoodAmigos as a provider with onboarding resources for customers who choose to move. That referral does not establish feature equivalence, Swiss availability or a particular migration outcome.

swissPayments.q: Which option should I choose for Swiss payments?
swissPayments.a: Start with the payment methods and processor your own restaurant needs, then verify eligibility, fees, settlement currency and setup in writing. Lightspeed’s Swiss page advertises TWINT; public sources reviewed here do not establish equivalent Swiss payment availability for every plan or provider.

switzerland.label: Restaurant field guide
switzerland.title: Set up a QR menu for a Swiss restaurant
switzerland.subtitle: A practical workflow for languages, prices, table codes and service handoff, written for the team that has to run it during a busy shift.
switzerland.intro: Switzerland has four national languages—German, French, Italian and Romansh—but that does not mean every restaurant should publish every menu in all four. Choose versions that match your location and guests, and that your team can keep accurate.
switzerland.stepsTitle: Work through the setup in this order

languages.title: Choose languages your team can maintain
languages.body: Start with the language your guests expect at this location, then add versions that match your actual customer mix. In German-speaking Switzerland, everyday dialects vary; standard German is used for written communication. Keep dish names, descriptions and modifiers consistent across each published version.

currency.title: Set one price source of truth
currency.body: Choose the menu currency deliberately—CHF is the common starting point for a Swiss restaurant—and check that item prices, add-ons, receipts and online checkout agree. If a payment provider settles in another currency or charges separately, confirm that before launch.

qrFlow.title: Decide what the QR code should do
qrFlow.body: Choose whether it opens a browse-only menu, starts an order, or also offers online payment. Map each table code to the intended table, then confirm what happens after a guest submits an order and where staff see it.

menuData.title: Translate the full choice, not just the headings
menuData.body: Review dish names, descriptions, sizes, modifiers, extras, sold-out status and the allergen information your kitchen maintains in every language. Assign one menu owner to publish changes together so one language does not quietly fall behind.

rehearsal.title: Rehearse one complete service path
rehearsal.body: Scan each code on a real phone, open the right language, change an option and submit a test order. Check table identification, kitchen or printer routing, displayed prices, receipts and the staff fallback if Wi-Fi, a phone or the ordering flow fails.

fieldCheck.title: Before you print every code
fieldCheck.body: Keep a short table-to-code list. After changing a menu, table number, price or payment setting, scan a printed code again and confirm it still opens the intended live menu.

geneva.label: Geneva restaurant field guide
geneva.title: A French-first QR menu workflow for Geneva
geneva.subtitle: Use French as the menu’s starting point, then add the languages your guests need and your team can keep current.
geneva.intro: French is the official language of the Republic and Canton of Geneva. For a restaurant operating in Geneva, a French-first menu is a practical starting point; choose additional guest languages from the people you serve and the translations your team can maintain.
geneva.stepsTitle: Build the guest and staff workflow

language.title: Make French the clear starting point
language.body: Set French as the default menu and keep a visible language selector. Add English or other languages where they serve real guests. Switzerland’s four national languages are not a reason to turn on every version for every restaurant.

menu.title: Complete the French source menu first
menu.body: Check dish names, descriptions, portions, modifiers and extras in French, then translate the whole choice into each enabled language. Keep item availability and the allergen information your kitchen tracks aligned across versions.

tables.title: Give every table the right code
tables.body: Print a code for each intended table and scan it from the guest side. If guests can order, confirm the submitted ticket reaches staff with the correct table identifier; if the code is browse-only, make the next step obvious.

service.title: Test a real shift, including the fallback
service.body: Have staff and a guest try the menu on their phones in French and each enabled language. Rehearse a change or sold-out item, a dine-in order, payment if enabled, kitchen or printer handoff, and how staff help when scanning or connectivity fails.

maintain.title: Keep changes synchronized
maintain.body: Assign one person to own the menu. When a price, modifier or dish changes, update every language before publishing; periodically scan printed codes and remove old ones when tables or links change.

fieldCheck.title: A real Geneva reference
fieldCheck.body: SofraPiwas publishes RUMI, a Geneva restaurant, as a customer case study. It is a product example, not a claim about measured business results.
